slides.say: A circle with center O has a radius of ten centimeters. The highlighted arc A B is four pi centimeters long. What is alpha?

We could put the numbers into the arc-length formula. Alpha over three hundred sixty, times two pi r, equals four pi, and so on. If that confused you a little, great, because we don't need it. [short pause] We'll see which part of the circle the arc is.
We know the arc is four pi, and the radius is ten. So let's find the whole circumference. Two pi r is two pi times ten, which is twenty pi.

So the whole circle is twenty pi, and the arc is four pi. Four pi out of twenty pi is like four out of twenty, which is a fifth. So the arc is a fifth of the circle. Five arcs like it go all the way around.
at: Four pi out of twenty pi

slides.say: And if the arc is a fifth of the circle, its central angle is also a fifth of the full turn. A fifth of three hundred sixty is seventy-two. So alpha is seventy-two degrees, choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: its central angle is also a fifth
